deals.proximityHighways: Intersection of Broadway Street and Trenton Road (combined 11,300 AADT) in Browns Mills, Pemberton Township. Roughly 25 miles south of Trenton, 30 miles east of Philadelphia and 30 miles from the Jersey Shore.
deals.retailCotenants: Immediately adjacent to a 38,000 SF ACME Markets — the only ACME within 10 miles and the #1 busiest grocer of 16 in the 10-mile trade area, with ±819,500 annual customer visits. Major employment nearby: the Deborah Heart and Lung Center (1,370 employees, contiguous to the property) and Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst (42,000+ active-duty, civilian and family members) six miles north. The obsolete former Browns Mills Shopping Center down Broadway Street was demolished in May 2026 to make way for a new Tractor Supply, Wawa and Taco Bell.
deals.shadowAnchors: ACME Markets — a 38,000 SF store in a building CONTIGUOUS to Pine Grove Plaza, not owned and not part of the offering. ACME has served Browns Mills since 1962 and relocated to this building in 2001 from the now-demolished Browns Mills Shopping Center. It is the only ACME within a 10-mile radius and ranks #1 of 16 grocers in the 10-mile trade area by traffic, at ±819,500 annual visits. Ownership holds no lease, no term and no go-dark protection over it — the grocery traffic underpinning the in-line rents is entirely uncontracted.

keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), which is what the $773,224 in-place NOI, the $273,615 recovery line and the $1,191,176 effective gross revenue tie to. This OM prints FULL lease dates (MM/DD/YY). Where the page-4 site plan shows a lower CURRENT rate, that rate is recorded in each tenant's rentSchedule.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) 71,306 SF occupied + 8,000 SF vacant = 79,306 SF GLA; (b) 71,306 / 79,306 = 89.9% occupancy; (c) base rents sum to $916,561 vs the $916,560 printed (rounding); (d) $1,191,176 EGR - $417,951 OpEx = $773,225 vs the $773,224 NOI printed (rounding). Tenant recoveries sum to $273,615 exactly.

WALT computes to 4.32 years from the roster's CURRENT-TERM expiries SF-weighted as of 01/01/2027, reproducing the OM's stated +/-4.3 years. Note this excludes Ollie's three five-year options, which would carry that anchor to a potential 2045.

ACME MARKETS IS NOT PART OF THE OFFERING. The 38,000 SF grocer sits in a CONTIGUOUS building that ownership does not own, appears nowhere on the rent roll, and contributes no rent or CAM to the income statement. It is the trade area's dominant grocer — only ACME within 10 miles, #1 of 16 by traffic, ±819,500 annual visits, in Browns Mills since 1962 — and the in-line rents depend on the traffic it generates, but there is no lease, no term and no go-dark protection behind that dependence.

OLLIE'S CONTRIBUTES ZERO EXPENSE RECOVERY on 31.5% of the GLA. That is the single largest structural item in the deal's expense side and is why the center recovers only $273,615 against $417,951 of operating expenses — a 65% recovery ratio. Confirm the structure against the lease before underwriting any expense growth or tax reassessment.

THE $1,000 STARLIGHT MEDIA LICENCE is a month-to-month signage/media agreement, modeled flat across all eleven years. It sits inside the EGR and therefore inside the NOI. Immaterial at 0.1%, but it is cancellable and should not be capitalized like rent.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $773,224 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED, AND THIS IS NEW JERSEY. The $191,133 CY2027 real-estate tax line is $2.41/SF and 25% of NOI — the second-heaviest tax burden in this portfolio group — and the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. New Jersey municipalities revalue on their own schedules and a sale is a common trigger for an assessor's attention; Pemberton Township's revaluation status and the property's current assessment-to-true-value ratio should be confirmed before bidding. With Ollie's recovering nothing on 31.5% of the GLA, a meaningful share of any increase lands directly on ownership.

THE MARKET-RENT ASSUMPTIONS LOOK OPTIMISTIC AGAINST THE CENTER'S OWN RECENT SIGNINGS. CBRE assumes $22.00/SF for 2,000-4,000 SF space, but P.Y. Kitchen signed in October 2026 — three months before the analysis period — at $13.00/SF on a nine-year term. Wright Fight Concepts signed May 2024 at $16.97/SF and Wireless Zone August 2024 at $21.00/SF, both under the $24.00/SF assumed for sub-2,000 SF space. Weigh the actual signings, not the assumption sheet, when underwriting the 8,000 SF vacancy at $15.00/SF.

MCDONALD'S IS A GROUND LEASE and a candidate for parcelization/spin-off, but the OM discloses no purchase option, right of first refusal or right of first offer. McDonald's ground leases frequently carry an ROFR on a pad sale. Do not assume a spin-off is available until the executed lease is read — flag this to counsel.

The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, individual rent steps, renewal-option terms other than Ollie's, or any co-tenancy, exclusive or kickout clause. All left null rather than estimated. No footer date stamp appears on the Pine Grove pro-forma pages, so omDate is left null (the sister Project Evergreen books are stamped July-August 2026).

redFlags.description: THE GROCER IS NOT OWNED AND IS NOT IN THE DEAL. ACME Markets — 38,000 SF, the only ACME within 10 miles, #1 of 16 grocers in the trade area by traffic, ±819,500 annual visits — occupies a contiguous building that ownership does not control. It generates the traffic the entire in-line roster depends on, and the deal has no lease, no term, no go-dark clause and no recapture right over it. That is the structural risk here, and it is not priced in the OM's framing of the asset as 'shadow anchored.'

OLLIE'S RECOVERS NOTHING ON 31.5% OF THE GLA. The anchor contributes $0 of expense reimbursement, so the center recovers $273,615 against $417,951 of operating expenses — a 65% recovery ratio. On a New Jersey asset carrying $191,133 of real-estate taxes ($2.41/SF, 25% of NOI) that gap is expensive today and gets worse with every expense increase or reassessment.

CBRE'S MARKET RENTS ARE CONTRADICTED BY THE CENTER'S OWN RECENT LEASES. The assumption sheet uses $22.00/SF for 2,000-4,000 SF space, but P.Y. Kitchen signed in October 2026 — three months before the projection starts — at $13.00/SF on a nine-year term, a 41% gap. Wright Fight signed May 2024 at $16.97/SF against a $24.00/SF assumption. The 8,000 SF vacancy is underwritten at $15.00/SF with $40/SF of TI; if actual rents land where the recent signings did, the modeled 45.9% ten-year NOI growth is overstated.

10.1% OF GLA IS VACANT IN A SINGLE 8,000 SF BLOCK — a junior-box leasing task, not small-shop fill, in a small Burlington County community. CBRE models it absorbed in one event on 1/1/2028 at $15.00/SF on a 10-year term with $40/SF of TI (roughly $320,000) and 9 months of downtime. The CY2028 capital line carries $354,320 of TI plus $113,360 of commissions, and NOI growing from $773,224 to $919,324 depends on that single lease landing.

TWO OF THE THREE HIGHEST RENTS LOOK ABOVE MARKET WITH NO SALES TO SUPPORT THEM. Mills Veterinary Care pays $28.18/SF against CBRE's own $22.00/SF assumption for that size — 28% above — and T-Mobile pays $24.97/SF against the same $22.00/SF, with T-Mobile EXPIRING OCTOBER 2027 in year one with no disclosed option. Above-market rent on a near-term expiry resets down; treat the $53,924 as at risk rather than as durable income.

NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ANY TENANT AT THE CENTER. Not one of the seventeen occupied suites has productivity data — including Ollie's, Dollar Tree and the two above-market shop rents. Tenant health simply cannot be assessed from this book.

Near-term rollover is front-loaded and unprotected: Hair Cuttery (July 2027), T-Mobile (October 2027), Rent-A-Center (March 2028), Anytime Fitness (February 2028) and H&R Block (April 2028) — 13,560 SF and roughly $236,000 of base rent — all expire within about sixteen months of the analysis start with no disclosed options, and CBRE's in-place NOI assumes they simply hold over at current rents.

The roster is heavily franchised and local-operator: Anytime Fitness, H&R Block, Wireless Zone, Wright Fight Concepts, D&F Foods and possibly McDonald's and T-Mobile are all likely franchisee or dealer entities rather than corporate credit, and no guaranties are disclosed. The OM's '44.5% of revenue from national credit tenants' claim should be tested lease by lease.

McDonald's ground lease is presented as parcelizable optionality, but no ROFR, ROFO or purchase option is disclosed. McDonald's pad leases commonly carry one, and it would block a spin-off. Read the lease before crediting that value.

upsideItems.item: Lease up the single 8,000 SF vacancy
upsideItems.detail: Lease up the single 8,000 SF vacancy (10.1% of GLA). CBRE models it absorbed 1/1/2028 at $15.00/SF on a 10-year NNN term, taking NOI from $773,224 to $919,324 — nearly the whole of the modeled CY2028 step. Budget the ~$320,000 of tenant improvements and $113,360 of commissions, and stress-test the $15.00/SF against P.Y. Kitchen's actual October 2026 signing at $13.00/SF.

upsideItems.item: 30.3% of GLA rolls inside the hold
upsideItems.detail: 24,003 SF (30.3% of GLA) expires during the hold, which is the OM's stated mark-to-market window. In-place rent is $12.85/SF against CBRE's $14.37/SF 2027 weighted-average market rent, and the modeled cash flow reaches $1,128,437 of NOI by CY2036 — 45.9% growth over the in-place figure.

upsideItems.item: Ollie's options run to a potential 2045
upsideItems.detail: Ollie's holds three additional five-year options to a potential 2045, which is exceptional term security on 31.5% of the GLA from a growing national discount retailer. The $8.00/SF rent is actually above CBRE's $6.00/SF junior-anchor market assumption, so this is fairly-priced, durable income rather than upside — its value is that it makes the rest of the business plan financeable.

upsideItems.item: Parcelize and spin off the McDonald's ground lease
upsideItems.detail: The McDonald's ground lease is a genuine structuring lever: $80,525 of ground rent on a separately identifiable pad, in place since 2000, running to October 2031, with CBRE modeling a $30.00/SF pad market rent against $23.01/SF in place. A parcelized McDonald's ground lease trades far tighter than an 89.9%-leased Burlington County strip — subject to confirming there is no ROFR.

Genuinely strong trade-area income for a small community: $107,839 average household income within three miles ($84,403 median) and $111,966 across the true trade area. Combined with a constrained, semi-rural supply picture, that supports the shop rents better than the population count alone suggests.

upsideItems.item: Deborah Heart & Lung and Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst
upsideItems.detail: Two large, stable employment anchors: the Deborah Heart and Lung Center with 1,370 employees is CONTIGUOUS to the property, and Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst with 42,000+ active-duty, civilian and family members sits six miles north — daytime demand that is largely recession- and e-commerce-insensitive.

upsideItems.item: New Tractor Supply, Wawa and Taco Bell in the node
upsideItems.detail: The retail node is visibly improving: the obsolete former Browns Mills Shopping Center down Broadway Street was demolished in May 2026 to make way for a Tractor Supply, Wawa and Taco Bell — new national investment that validates the node and adds traffic without adding directly competing shop space.

upsideItems.item: Two large suites are locked well below market
upsideItems.detail: Happy Taps Spirits at $10.00/SF and Community Dental at $8.00/SF sit far below CBRE's $16.50/SF assumption for space that size. Both recover $6.37/SF on top and both run to 2034-2035, so the spread is secure income rather than capturable upside — but it means the in-place rent roll is not carrying hidden downside on those 9,840 SF.

deals.notes: Pine Grove Plaza is a 79,306 SF neighborhood center at Broadway Street and Trenton Road in Browns Mills, Pemberton Township, New Jersey, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is 89.9% leased and produces $773,224 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $1,191,176 of effective gross revenue against $417,951 of operating expenses, at a $12.85/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $14.37/SF modeled market rent. The owned anchor is a 24,963 SF Ollie's Bargain Outlet at $8.00/SF with a current term to October 2030 and three five-year options to a potential 2045; Dollar Tree, Rent-A-Center, McDonald's on a ground lease, Anytime Fitness and H&R Block round out a genuinely daily-needs roster. The traffic thesis, however, rests on a 38,000 SF ACME Markets that is NOT part of the offering — it occupies a contiguous building ownership does not control, is the only ACME within ten miles and the busiest of sixteen grocers in the trade area, and comes with no lease, no term and no go-dark protection whatsoever. Two other items shape the underwriting. Ollie's contributes zero expense reimbursement on 31.5% of the GLA, leaving a 65% recovery ratio against a New Jersey tax line of $191,133 — $2.41/SF and 25% of NOI — that CBRE expressly did not reassess. And the market rents behind the growth case look optimistic against the center's own recent deals: CBRE assumes $22.00/SF for mid-size shop space, but P.Y. Kitchen signed in October 2026, three months before the projection begins, at $13.00/SF on a nine-year term. The value-add case is the single 8,000 SF vacancy plus 24,003 SF rolling during the hold, and the parcelizable McDonald's ground lease is real optionality if no right of first refusal blocks it. The trade area supports the plan better than its size suggests — $107,839 average household income within three miles, the 1,370-employee Deborah Heart and Lung Center contiguous to the property, Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst six miles north, and a new Tractor Supply, Wawa and Taco Bell replacing the demolished center down the street.
